Q: What does transitive = true in Gradle exactly do (w.r.t. crashlytics)? A:

On a more general note: Setting transitive = false on the crashlytics library causes gradle to ignore all libraries required by crashlytics (="transient libraries") and not download and link them.

You would have to either manually add the required libraries to your project or rely on other transient libraries added by other dependencies.

Default for gradle is transitive = true.

Examples and full explanation here: http://www.devsbedevin.com/android-understanding-gradle-dependencies-and-resolving-conflicts/

Q: How can I force Gradle to set the same version for two dependencies? A:

I would suggest against setting transitive = false, as this approach would force yo to resolve the dependency tree yourself, manually.

You could either force the desired guava version via configurations.all, or add the dependency explicitly and set it forced = true.

Examples here: http://www.devsbedevin.com/android-understanding-gradle-dependencies-and-resolving-conflicts/

Q: Android emulator proxy setting A:

I've recently had to set up a sniffing environment to debug some Android SSL traffic.

It seems now that you no longer need to set the proxy on the emulator's access point (steps 2-4 on @craig-russell's answer). Adding the -http-proxy launch parameter is enough. Also tried on API levels < 23 and succeeded.

My specs: Android Studio 2.3.1 Windows 10 Android emulator version 25.2.5.0

Full details: http://www.devsbedevin.com/debugging-android-ssl-traffic/
